lines.text: Forty million Americans live with diabetes. A hundred and fifteen million adults have prediabetes. And for all of them, every meal is the same question: does this fit my day?
Meet Maya, who has insulin resistance, and Daniel, who has type 2 diabetes. Made up, but you know them. She has no time. He has a plan that keeps breaking.
Wrap and chips. Is that okay? I honestly don't know.
Maya has no time to plan, so she guesses. Most tools ask for a life with spare time.
Sunday. The whole week, planned.
Daniel plans every meal.
Wednesday. A late meeting. Pizza.
Then life happens, and a broken plan feels like failing.
That is why DiaBite exists. Say what you are about to eat. It tells you if it fits what is left of your day, and shows the arithmetic.
Grilled chicken sandwich and an apple.
A few seconds. It fits, but it names a lighter swap, and counts that too.
Chicken salad instead. Fine.
Every number comes from a database. Open the receipt and check it yourself.
In the diary, his plan stays, dashed. Only what he really eats counts.
Chicken fried rice.
A plan that broke is not a failure. It is just Wednesday.
How many units of insulin before pasta?
Some questions it never answers. Doses belong to your care team.
Grandma's cholent.
And when it does not know a dish, it says so, and calls it an estimate.
A quick check on the go. A diary for the days a plan breaks. Free to try at diabite.pro. A reference tool, not medical advice.
